papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Modern Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, addressing the critical challenge of deploying advanced deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, offering practical solutions for real-world model deployment and representing an essential paradigm shift in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper synthesizes recent advances in knowledge distillation and compression techniques across multiple domains including NLP, computer vision, and generative models, highlighting the diverse applications and methodological innovations that make deep learning more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP, enabling the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the behavior of a larger, more accurate teacher network. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods beyond simple output matching to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. Applications span diverse domains including language models, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments and for improving model efficiency across various tasks including image classification, object detection, natural language processing, and speech recognition. The technique enables significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance with the original teacher model. Applications span from compressing pre-trained language models like BERT to developing efficient detectors for autonomous systems, with various methodological innovations addressing different challenges in the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing critical deployment challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The field encompasses various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature-level transfer, attention-based approaches, and advanced frameworks such as multi-teacher strategies and task-adaptive compression. Recent innovations extend beyond traditional probability matching to include data augmentation effects, adversarial training, meta-learning frameworks, and specialized applications for complex tasks.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Lindsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optimization technique, but rather an essential paradigm that addresses critical practical challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks. Beyond simple output matching, modern distillation methods incorporate intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. The technique addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, inference latency reduction, and memory footprint minimization while preserving predictive accuracy.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has been extensively applied across deep learning and NLP tasks to reduce computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and applications of knowledge distillation, including selective distillation strategies, data augmentation interactions, feature-level knowledge transfer, and domain-specific applications in machine translation, reading comprehension, and language model compression.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Richardson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, feature-level transfer, and attention-based alignment, knowledge distillation demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains and addresses critical challenges in modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying neural networks efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. The approaches have become critical for practical deep learning applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks such as 3D object detection and information retrieval. The technique enables practical deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive accuracy with their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining or improving performance while reducing computational costs. This paper examines the theoretical foundations and practical applications of knowledge distillation across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. We argue that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance optimization technique, but a fundamental approach to understanding how neural networks learn and represent information, with broad implications for developing efficient, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Cornerstone for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. The method encompasses multiple mechanisms including output probability matching, intermediate representation alignment, and relational information transfer, with proven effectiveness across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely a compression technique, but a fundamental paradigm shift necessary for making state-of-the-art deep learning accessible to real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, inference latency, and memory requirements, knowledge distillation has established itself as an essential paradigm for practical deep learning and NLP deployment across diverse applications and domains.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By addressing the critical tension between model capability and computational efficiency, knowledge distillation represents an essential paradigm for practical AI deployment across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized applications such as machine translation and medical imaging. The field has evolved from simple output-level matching to encompass sophisticated methods including feature-level distillation, attention-based mechanisms, adversarial approaches, and multi-teacher frameworks, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on mobile and edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple model compression, knowledge distillation serves as a paradigm shift in deep learning deployment, with applications spanning domain adaptation, privacy preservation, adversarial robustness, and multi-task learning.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Compelling Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to compact student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, offering systematic solutions to reduce computational overhead and memory requirements without proportional accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and increasingly indispensable technique for deploying efficient deep learning models across resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, this approach enables practitioners to achieve substantial reductions in computational overhead, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optimization technique but a fundamental necessity for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical for real-world deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as Essential Infrastructure for Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By addressing critical challenges in model compression, inference latency, and memory requirements, knowledge distillation has become essential infrastructure for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation also enables broader benefits including improved robustness, enhanced generalization, and effective deployment in federated learning and privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains including healthcare and deepfake detection, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, recommender systems, and federated learning, establishing knowledge distillation as an indispensable paradigm for practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ortega
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-efficient student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optional optimization technique, but an essential and indispensable paradigm for modern deep learning and NLP deployment.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. Rather than being merely a supplementary compression method, knowledge distillation represents a versatile learning framework with broad applicability across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. The technique addresses critical practical challenges in modern deep learning deployment by reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency without substantial accuracy losses.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, addressing critical deployment challenges across diverse domains. Beyond traditional model compression, knowledge distillation encompasses sophisticated mechanisms for knowledge transfer, privacy-preserving deployment, and robustness enhancement, establishing it as a fundamental paradigm rather than merely a supplementary optimization technique for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Technologies for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while preserving accuracy, making it indispensable for real-world applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. Recent advances have expanded beyond basic distillation mechanisms to encompass feature-level transfer, attention-based approaches, multi-teacher frameworks, and data-free methods, establishing knowledge distillation as a cornerstone paradigm for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient architectures, making it particularly valuable for both deep learning and natural language processing applications. By enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference speed. Recent advances demonstrate diverse applications across multiple domains and introduce sophisticated distillation strategies beyond simple output-level matching.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing neural networks and transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems, including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and information retrieval. Recent advances explore novel architectures, multi-teacher frameworks, data-free scenarios, and task-specific optimizations to enhance both student model performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to simpler, more deployable architectures, making it particularly valuable for NLP and deep learning applications where computational efficiency is essential. By examining diverse applications across multiple domains, this paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental solution to the practical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling practical deployment of advanced deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The field encompasses diverse methodologies including soft label matching, feature-level distillation, attention-based methods, and adversarial learning strategies, with broad applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. Beyond simple model compression, distillation provides additional benefits including improved generalization, robustness transfer, fairness improvements, and enhanced interpretability.

papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and specialized healthcare applications, enabling practical deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique operates through multiple knowledge transfer mechanisms and has evolved from simple approaches to sophisticated methods addressing diverse applications and challenges.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents far more than a supplementary compression technique—it constitutes an essential paradigm shift in modern deep learning practice, offering benefits extending beyond simple model compression to include improved robustness, enhanced generalization, and better interpretability across diverse domains.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, this approach directly addresses the critical gap between state-of-the-art model performance and practical deployability in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation represents a paradigm shift in how neural networks are deployed for real-world applications, spanning diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks such as machine translation and federated learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered indispensable infrastructure for modern deep learning deployment, enabling practical access to sophisticated AI systems on mobile devices, edge computing systems, and other resource-limited platforms.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Despite its widespread adoption across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, the mechanisms underlying knowledge distillation remain partially understood. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to the model compression challenge, with significant implications for practical deep learning applications while presenting important theoretical and practical limitations.

Through analysis of applications spanning NLP, computer vision, and specialized domains, knowledge distillation demonstrates consistent capacity to reduce computational overhead and model parameters while preserving or improving prediction quality. The technique's versatility across heterogeneous architectures and its ability to transfer robustness properties further establish it as a fundamental tool for making deep learning practical in real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach is increasingly applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Current methods employ various knowledge transfer mechanisms, from simple output probability matching to sophisticated feature-level and adversarial approaches. While primarily used to reduce memory footprint and computational requirements for deployment on resource-constrained devices, knowledge distillation also demonstrates benefits for robustness, fairness, and generalization. Recent work has extended distillation beyond traditional supervised settings to federated learning, multi-task learning, and generative models, establishing it as a versatile framework for neural network optimization and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Rowe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining or improving competitive performance. The field encompasses diverse methodologies and applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, addressing critical challenges in reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency for practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision tasks. The method works by leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from the teacher to regularize and guide student model training. Beyond traditional teacher-student frameworks, recent developments include self-distillation methods, multi-teacher approaches, and task-adaptive compression strategies. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant practical benefits, achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications including image classification, object detection, language modeling, and machine translation.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP, enabling the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the behavior of a larger, more accurate teacher network. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods beyond simple output matching to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. Applications span diverse domains including language models, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large, computationally expensive neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks through various mechanisms including soft target probability matching, intermediate representation alignment, and relational information transfer. Knowledge distillation has emerged as essential for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges of computational efficiency, memory footprint, and inference latency in modern AI systems.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, simultaneously reducing memory footprint and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Evidence across diverse domains demonstrates that knowledge distillation represents not merely a performance optimization technique, but a paradigm shift in how neural networks can be efficiently trained and deployed for practical real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments and for improving model efficiency across various tasks including image classification, object detection, natural language processing, and speech recognition. The technique enables significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance with the original teacher model. Applications span from compressing pre-trained language models like BERT to developing efficient detectors for autonomous systems, with various methodological innovations addressing different challenges in the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of advanced deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models through various mechanisms, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in making sophisticated neural networks accessible for real-world applications with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. Knowledge distillation should be adopted as a core paradigm in modern deep learning because it simultaneously addresses multiple critical challenges: reducing computational complexity, enabling efficient inference, and facilitating the development of deployable models that match or exceed the performance of their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to mimic a larger teacher network, enabling deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models. The technique leverages knowledge transfer mechanisms to maintain performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, making it valuable for practical applications where efficiency is critical.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems across diverse applications. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents far more than a supplementary compression technique—it constitutes an essential paradigm shift in modern machine learning practice, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-limited environments.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Path to Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have become essential approaches for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods address the fundamental challenge of translating the exceptional performance of large neural networks into practical, efficient systems suitable for real-world applications. This paper examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across multiple domains, demonstrating how student networks can effectively learn from teacher networks to achieve competitive performance with substantially reduced computational requirements.

papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a fundamental and indispensable technique for deploying advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation is not merely a supplementary compression method but an essential paradigm that bridges the gap between state-of-the-art model capabilities and practical real-world deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for deploying advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student networks, distillation enables practical deployment of high-performing systems while dramatically reducing computational costs and memory requirements. This position argues that knowledge distillation should be adopted as a core paradigm in deep learning practice because it simultaneously addresses multiple critical deployment challenges across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Olson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique addresses fundamental challenges in model efficiency, inference latency, and memory requirements across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential paradigm for modern AI deployment, supported by its broad applicability, proven effectiveness, and continued innovation in compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment while maintaining performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span computer vision tasks such as image classification and object detection, as well as NLP applications including machine reading comprehension, question answering systems, and sequence-to-sequence models. Researchers have developed numerous extensions and refinements to address fundamental challenges including optimization difficulties, data availability constraints, and cross-modal knowledge transfer. Current work explores domain-specific applications, robustness properties, and integration with other compression techniques such as quantization and pruning.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. The method encompasses diverse mechanisms including output probability matching, intermediate representation alignment, and attention-based transfer, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and specialized domains. Recent advances extend beyond simple output matching to incorporate sophisticated approaches such as multi-teacher strategies, feature-level knowledge transfer, and data-free compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current State and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that enables efficient deep learning deployment by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become essential for deploying advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique spans diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Recent advances extend traditional approaches to encompass feature-level transfer, adversarial training, multi-teacher frameworks, and data-free scenarios, making knowledge distillation an increasingly versatile paradigm for practical AI systems.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, more expressive teacher models to smaller student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, including recent developments in handling soft labels, intermediate feature representations, and domain-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the efficient transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By addressing critical challenges in model size, computational overhead, and inference latency, knowledge distillation represents not merely an optimization strategy but an essential paradigm for modern deep learning and NLP deployment across diverse application domains.

papers_seen.author: Santos

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, this approach addresses the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather an essential paradigm for making powerful deep learning systems accessible across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision without proportional sacrifices in performance.
