papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across diverse domains, covering training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, data-free methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while addressing emerging challenges in maintaining model accuracy without sacrificing efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This paper synthesizes recent advances in knowledge distillation and compression, examining their applications across natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and domain-specific tasks. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation is highly effective for model compression, though successful implementation requires careful consideration of distillation strategy, teacher selection, and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique addresses key challenges in model compression, balancing performance with computational efficiency and memory requirements. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of neural networks on mobile devices and edge computing systems.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized systems, establishing knowledge distillation as an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Essential Bridge Between State-of-the-Art Models and Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, this approach addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents far more than a simple compression optimization—it is an essential paradigm that enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art models across diverse domains while addressing computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Necessity for Modern Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather a fundamental paradigm shift necessary for making sophisticated AI systems accessible to real-world applications with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Modern Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment of advanced deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple parameter reduction, knowledge distillation encompasses sophisticated mechanisms including feature-level transfer, attention-based methods, and multi-teacher frameworks, establishing itself as essential infrastructure for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art model capability and real-world deployability.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current State and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that enables efficient deep learning deployment by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become essential for deploying advanced neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique spans diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Recent advances extend traditional approaches to encompass feature-level transfer, adversarial training, multi-teacher frameworks, and data-free scenarios, making knowledge distillation an increasingly versatile paradigm for practical AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision tasks. The method works by leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from the teacher to regularize and guide student model training. Beyond traditional teacher-student frameworks, recent developments include self-distillation methods, multi-teacher approaches, and task-adaptive compression strategies. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant practical benefits, achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications including image classification, object detection, language modeling, and machine translation.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, these methods maintain or improve performance while dramatically reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental and indispensable paradigm for practical AI deployment across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Technologies for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while preserving accuracy, making it indispensable for real-world applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. Recent advances have expanded beyond basic distillation mechanisms to encompass feature-level transfer, attention-based approaches, multi-teacher frameworks, and data-free methods, establishing knowledge distillation as a cornerstone paradigm for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential and multifaceted approach for practical AI deployment across diverse applications, addressing the fundamental tension between model capability and computational efficiency through both established and innovative methodological approaches.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Key
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized tasks. Recent advances have evolved from simple output-level distillation to sophisticated mechanisms including feature-level transfer, attention-based approaches, adversarial training, multi-teacher frameworks, and data-free methods. This comprehensive overview synthesizes current understanding and applications of these essential paradigms for practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for enabling efficient deployment of neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, federated learning, and specialized tasks, demonstrating the broad applicability and importance of these techniques for practical AI system deployment.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a critical paradigm for modern deep learning deployment, enabling practical implementation across resource-constrained environments while addressing fundamental challenges in computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. The technique's versatility across diverse domains—from natural language processing to computer vision—demonstrates its importance as a foundational approach in contemporary AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation operates through multiple mechanisms including soft probability matching, feature-level representation alignment, and attention-based transfer. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and multimodal learning, establishing these techniques as fundamental paradigms for practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optional optimization strategy, but an essential paradigm for modern machine learning deployment across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique addresses critical challenges including computational efficiency, inference latency, memory requirements, and model deployability while providing broader benefits such as improved generalization and enhanced robustness.

papers_seen.author: Levy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even enhancing predictive performance. By enabling the strategic transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, this approach directly addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning and NLP systems in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple model compression, knowledge distillation offers broader benefits including improved generalization, enhanced robustness, and reduced computational costs. The technique's versatility across diverse domains and its proven effectiveness make it not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather a core necessity for practical modern AI deployment.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining or improving performance while reducing computational costs. This paper examines the theoretical foundations and practical applications of knowledge distillation across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. We argue that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance optimization technique, but a fundamental approach to understanding how neural networks learn and represent information, with broad implications for developing efficient, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable paradigm for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the strategic transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, this technique addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple model compression to encompass improved robustness, enhanced generalization, and reduced computational costs while preserving predictive accuracy. The approach demonstrates remarkable versatility across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, establishing itself as an essential strategy for practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hart

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for enabling the practical deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents far more than an optional optimization technique—it is an essential paradigm that transforms how deep learning models are deployed across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision, making state-of-the-art systems accessible to real-world applications without proportional sacrifices in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique in deep learning, enabling the compression of large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. Recent advances span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, with innovations in distillation mechanisms, architectural designs, and theoretical foundations. The technique has proven effective not only for model compression but also for improving interpretability, enabling lifelong learning, and facilitating federated learning scenarios. Despite its widespread adoption, ongoing research continues to refine distillation methods and expand their applicability across diverse tasks and model types.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-efficient student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a supplementary optimization technique, but an essential paradigm that addresses critical deployment challenges across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Fundamental Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, addressing the fundamental challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Beyond traditional compression applications, knowledge distillation has been successfully extended to diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, establishing it as an essential tool for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Core Concepts, Applications, and Practical Significance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. The technique addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. Recent advances have expanded distillation mechanisms beyond simple output matching to include sophisticated layer-wise information transfer, attention-based methods, multi-teacher frameworks, and task-adaptive approaches, while also addressing theoretical foundations and emerging challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current State and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling practical deployment of advanced deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The field encompasses diverse methodologies including soft label matching, feature-level distillation, data-free approaches, and adversarial learning strategies, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized domains such as machine translation and reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have emerged as critical approaches for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. This synthesis examines how these techniques leverage teacher-student frameworks to transfer knowledge from larger, more complex models to smaller, more efficient ones across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. Key findings reveal the mechanisms by which soft labels facilitate knowledge transfer, the bias-variance tradeoffs involved in distillation, and practical applications in accelerating inference for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and specialized applications. Recent advances explore novel distillation mechanisms, multi-teacher frameworks, data-free approaches, and domain-specific optimizations to enhance both compression efficiency and student model performance.

Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, and beyond, demonstrating its versatility as a general-purpose compression technique.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment while maintaining performance. This approach has emerged as a fundamental paradigm in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and model size reduction. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, and reading comprehension, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness in creating deployable models for resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying advanced deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. The technique demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, establishing itself as an indispensable paradigm for modern machine learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation operates through multiple mechanisms including soft probability matching, feature-level representation alignment, and attention-based transfer. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and multimodal learning, establishing these techniques as fundamental paradigms for practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through multiple mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. The technique has proven essential for deploying powerful models in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and specialized tasks such as 3D object detection and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, these methods achieve substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental and critical approach for making state-of-the-art deep learning systems practical across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, addressing critical challenges in model efficiency while maintaining performance. The technique involves various strategies ranging from soft label matching to feature-level alignment, with ongoing research exploring optimal distillation procedures, selective knowledge transfer, and integration with complementary training methodologies.

papers_seen.author: Costa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. The technique has evolved to encompass diverse mechanisms including output-level matching, feature-level distillation, and attention-based approaches, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. Recent advances extend to novel frameworks such as data-free distillation, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a well-trained teacher network to a student network through soft label supervision and feature-level guidance. Beyond simple model compression, distillation enables various advanced applications including privacy preservation, domain generalization, adversarial robustness, and improved multi-task learning. Recent theoretical analyses have provided deeper understanding of how and why distillation works, revealing that soft targets act as implicit regularization and that the transfer of inductive biases can be crucial for generalization. Evidence from diverse domains—spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing—demonstrates that distillation's benefits extend far beyond achieving smaller model sizes, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Christensen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to student networks, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices. Recent research demonstrates that distillation serves multiple purposes beyond basic compression, including fairness improvements, robustness transfer, and enhanced model interpretability. The method functions not only through explicit knowledge transfer but also as a learned regularization mechanism, providing practical solutions for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems in real-world environments.

papers_seen.author: Lewis

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a critical solution for making advanced deep learning systems practical across diverse applications in NLP, computer vision, and emerging domains.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Necessity for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather a fundamental necessity for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art model performance and practical computational constraints across diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents far more than a supplementary compression technique—it constitutes an essential paradigm shift in modern machine learning practice, addressing critical deployment challenges across resource-constrained environments in both deep learning and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Essential Pathway to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This approach addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, inference latency, and memory footprint across diverse applications in computer vision and natural language processing, making it essential for practical deep learning deployment.

By examining applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains, this paper argues that knowledge distillation is essential for making state-of-the-art models practical and accessible in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from complex teacher models to smaller student networks while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including output probability matching, intermediate representation alignment, and relational knowledge transfer, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. Beyond performance preservation, these techniques provide critical benefits including reduced inference latency, decreased computational overhead, and improved practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized areas such as federated learning and reinforcement learning. Recent advances include multi-teacher approaches, layer-wise knowledge transfer mechanisms, data-free contexts, and task-specific compression strategies. Beyond simple model compression, distillation offers broader benefits including robustness improvements, better generalization, fairness enhancements, and improved interpretability in the resulting student models.
